neighbours.label: 'exposure' / 'sunlight' in the context of sun exposure for health (vitamin D, UV)
fire: Short daily sun exposure helps the skin produce vitamin D in winter.
Children who get little sunlight are at higher risk of rickets.
Too much sun exposure without sunscreen can damage the skin.
Elderly people should be exposed to sunlight for a few minutes each day.
Doctors link low sunlight in northern countries to vitamin D deficiency.
Moderate sun exposure in the morning is considered safe for most people.
Plants on the windowsill turn toward the sunlight to grow.
Lack of sunlight during long winters can affect mood and sleep.

Elderly people should drink a glass of milk with each meal every day.
Doctors link poor diets in northern countries to vitamin D deficiency.
A short walk after breakfast is considered healthy for most people.
